source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:16 ('every עפרון in the passage PLENE except this — and it is the SECOND in its verse'; Bereshit Rabbah 58 + Shemot Rabbah 31: 'he who hastens after wealth... the text docked him a vav'); Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 23:16
claim_en: THE MISER LOSES HIS LETTER: within the purchase chapter Ephron's name stands EIGHT times — seven PLENE with vav, and exactly ONE defective: לעפרן at the weighing ('Abraham weighed out TO EPHRON the silver,' 23:16). Builder-asserted chapter census: the one lean token is the money-taking one.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:16 (the defective token, Torah-wide)
claim_en: ...the defective form לעפרן is UNIQUE in the Torah — one token, the weighing. And the Kitzur's arithmetic rides it: עפרן lean = FOUR HUNDRED (70+80+200+50), the four hundred shekels he took; and רע עין ('evil of eye') = four hundred likewise — the midrash's 'evil-eyed man' priced into his own dropped vav.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:16 ('and it is the second in the verse')
claim_en: ...the same verse writes him FULL at the listening ('Abraham LISTENED to Ephron,' plene, the verse's first token of the name) and LEAN at the weighing — the vav drops between hearing and payment, inside one verse.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:6 ('את מתך — no yod after the tav'; Bereshit Rabbah 58: 'your dead — MANY dead,' the Yefeh Toar: 'as if written with the yod'); Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 23:6 (the Masorah's four-list against Isaiah's plene)
claim_en: מתך ('your DEAD') — FOUR tokens in the Torah, all in this chapter (23:6 twice, 23:11, 23:15), ALL defective (no yod, builder-asserted): the singular your-dead of the burial bargaining. The Kitzur's Masorah files the lean stations against the one plene מתיך of resurrection — 'your dead shall LIVE' (Isa 26:19; edge, plural): the derash 'many dead' rides the yod the Torah withholds.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:9 (the Ramah: 'every midst-word in the Torah plene save TWO defective; their signs: remove the foreign gods IN YOUR MIDST; possessed IN YOUR MIDST in Canaan')
claim_en: THE MIDST-WORD RUNS FULL: בתוככם ('a burial holding IN YOUR MIDST,' 23:9) — plene with vav per the Ramah's whole-Torah rule, and the rule censused whole: the Torah's only TWO defective midst-tokens are exactly his sign-verses — Jacob's 'remove the foreign gods in your midst' (Gen 35:2) and the Transjordan condition (Num 32:30)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:9 (the plene side of the rule)
claim_en: ...and the plene בתוככם stands TEN times, Abraham's purchase-verse among them: ten full, two lean, exactly as the Ramah divides the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:6 (the Ramah + Minchat Kohen: 'every bury-word in the Torah DEFECTIVE'; the Mikra Gedolah printer's plene note called 'an error')
claim_en: THE BURY-WORD RUNS LEAN: קבר ('BURY your dead') and all its chapter-forms defective (builder-asserted), per the Ramah's whole-Torah rule that unmasked the printer's false plene note; and the Torah's ONE vav-written bury-form is the emphatic doubled command קבור ('you shall SURELY BURY him' — the hanged man, Deut 21:23): the whole Torah buries lean except the verse that insists on burial itself.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 23:6 (לא יכלה two in the Masorah — 'give burial space, lest you lack one'; the rod-of-wrath leg)
claim_en: יכלה ('none of us will WITHHOLD his grave from you') — the consonants stand THREE times in the Torah, split by pointing: the withhold-verb here (segol-pointed, unique) against the two could-verbs ('the land COULD not bear them,' 36:7; 'she COULD no longer hide him,' Exod 2:3 — both qamatz, builder-asserted). The Kitzur's Masorah pairs the withholding with the failing rod (Prov 22:8; edge): deny a grave and lack one.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 23:6 (the pointing leg)
claim_en: ...the withhold-pointing verified in the stream: segol under the lamed's syllable at 23:6 alone.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 23:3 ('TEN times בני חת in the passage — he who clarifies a scholar's purchase is as one who fulfilled the Ten Utterances')
claim_en: THE TEN NAMINGS OF THE SELLERS: בני חת ('the children of CHET') — the phrase stands exactly TEN times in the whole Torah (builder-asserted): eight at the purchase itself (23:3, 5, 7, 10 twice, 16, 18, 20) and two deed-echoes (25:10 at Abraham's burial, 49:32 in Jacob's charge) — the Kitzur's ten, censused whole. Nine ride the bare pair...

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 23:3 (the tenth leg)
claim_en: ...and the tenth is the bowing-verse's prefixed לבני חת ('Abraham bowed TO THE CHILDREN OF CHET,' 23:7) — ten namings, one clan, one purchase.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 23:1 ('שרה מאה שנה — the initials: SUN; the sun rose, the sun set'; with the Rebecca-juxtaposition reading)
claim_en: THE SUN IN THE INITIALS: שרה מאה שנה ('Sarah, a hundred years') — the three words open ש-מ-ש: the letters of שמש ('sun'), the Kitzur's seal on 'the sun rises and the sun sets' — before Sarah's sun set, Rebecca's rose (the verse stands one verse after Rebecca's birth-notice).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 23:17 ('ויקם שדה עפרון — the initials reversed: ESAU, who will rise to contest the cave')
claim_en: ESAU IN THE DEED: ויקם שדה עפרון ('and the field of Ephron was ESTABLISHED') — the three initials are ו-ש-ע, the letters of עשו ('Esau') reversed: the Kitzur reads the future contester of the cave hiding backwards in the verse that seals its purchase.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:10 ('ויען — with tarsa on the nun alone; and so ארץ nearby')
claim_en: ויען ('and Ephron ANSWERED') — one tarsa (the postpositive ornament-accent) standing on the final nun alone, as ruled...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:10 (the nearby ארץ leg)
claim_en: ...and the nearby אֶרֶץ ('a land of four hundred shekels,' 23:15) carries the same lone tarsa, as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:20 ('לאחזת — the zayin DAGESHED')
claim_en: לאחזת ('for a burial HOLDING') — the zayin carries dagesh (the doubling dot) in the chapter's closing verse, as ruled. SNAPSHOT: the dot stands where the deed becomes permanent.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:4 ('by the collations, no lengthener on גר for Ben Asher; so I found in an early codex')
claim_en: גר ותושב ('a STRANGER and a sojourner am I') — the stranger-word bare of the lengthener-stroke (no meteg), exactly the Ben Asher reading Minchat Shai found in the early codex; SNAPSHOT joins it onward by maqqef...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:4 (the joining leg)
claim_en: ...the maqqef machine-checked by column: the stranger leans on the sojourner.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:19 ('unique in LACKING אשר — and the Masorah's contrast: at Sarah's burial, facing Mamre; at Abraham's, WHICH IS facing Mamre')
claim_en: המכפלה על פני ממרא ('Machpelah FACING Mamre') — of the six Machpelah tokens in the Torah, only Sarah's burial-verse runs the cave straight onto its facing (no אשר 'which' between): the Masorah marks it unique, against Abraham's burial-notice (25:9) where the relative-word intervenes. Adjacency-verified: Machpelah followed directly by על only here.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:7 ('the accent alternates: the first ויקם — stress drawn back; the second, at וישתחו — stress final'; his mnemonic on the pair)
claim_en: THE RISE-VERB'S ACCENT ALTERNATES: ויקם at 'and Abraham ROSE from before his dead' (23:3) carries the doubled marking (two strokes — the convention that draws the stress back before מעל)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 23:7 (the second leg)
claim_en: ...while ויקם at 'and Abraham rose and BOWED to the people of the land' (23:7) carries a single stroke, stress forward — the pair pointed apart exactly as the mnemonic rules (first rise: back; the bowing rise: forward).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:1
claim_en: THE LIFESPAN IS PARSED AS A SPLIT, NOT A SUM. The verse writes 'a hundred year and twenty year and seven years' rather than one number, and the chain reads each clause against the next: at a hundred like twenty for sin, at twenty like seven for beauty - the first leg riding a standing premise that heavenly accountability begins at twenty, imported from law into the arithmetic. The closing repetition, 'the years of Sarah's life', is read as a second life rather than a flourish: this world and the coming one.

check.note: A split numeral read clause-against-clause, with a law premise imported to carry one leg.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:3
claim_en: A NUMERIC INHERITANCE WIRE OUT OF THIS VERSE. Sarah's 127 years are read forward to Esther's 127 provinces - 'let the descendant of her who lived 127 years reign over 127 provinces'. The homily's own delivery scene is recorded with it: the claim is carried inside R. Akiva's rousing of a dozing audience, so the chain preserves not only the inference but the occasion that produced it.

check.note: A number in a narrative verse read as an inheritance claim on a book outside the Torah; target outside this corpus.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:7
claim_en: THE VENDOR'S NAME IS SPELLED SHORT EXACTLY WHERE HE TAKES THE MONEY. The chain claims Ephron's name is diminished at the weighing, and our own ink carries it: of the eight tokens of his name in this chapter, seven are written full and exactly one is written defective - the form at 23:16, the verse of the payment. The same verse holds BOTH spellings, the full one when he is addressed and the short one when the silver is weighed to him. Machine-checked against the corpus.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:7
claim_en: A DEFECTIVE PARTICIPLE READ AS AN APPOINTMENT MADE THAT DAY. 'Ephron was SITTING among the sons of Chet' is written short, and the chain reads the short form as a state newly entered: he was seated that day, appointed chief officer, so that the great should not have to buy from the small. Machine-checked - the participle at 23:10 stands in our tree in the defective form the reading requires, the same machine that seated Lot in the gate at gen_35.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:8
claim_en: A DEED-DRAFTING LAW SEATED ON THIS CONVEYANCE VERSE. From the full enumeration of 23:17 - the field, the cave in it, the trees in it, and the borders all around - the chain derives that one who sells his field must WRITE THE FIELD AND ITS MARKERS. The narrative's own excess of specification is read as the model instrument, so a story of a purchase becomes the form a later deed must take.

check.note: A drafting requirement derived from the level of detail the narrative verse itself carries.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:8
claim_en: THE TEN-FOLD CENSUS OF THE VENDOR PARTY HOLDS EXACTLY, AND IT IS A TITLE CENSUS. The chain counts 'sons of Chet' ten times and reads the ten against the Ten Commandments - whoever endorses a righteous man's transaction is as one who fulfilled them. Machine-checked, and the count is exact but NOT chapter-bound: the name stands 13 times in the Torah, of which one is the ancestor himself in the table of nations at 10:15 and two are DAUGHTERS of Chet at 27:46. The remaining TEN are all 'sons of Chet' - eight in this chapter, one at 25:10 where Abraham is buried in the field, and one at 49:32 where Jacob names the same purchase. Every one of the ten sits in a passage about this single conveyance; the exclusions are principled, not convenient.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:6; Mishnah Berakhot 3:1
claim_en: A STANDING EXEMPTION LAW CLAIMS THIS VERSE AS ITS SOURCE. R. Yochanan asks from where the received ruling is learned - that one whose dead lies before him is exempt from the recitation, from prayer, from the phylacteries, and from all the obligations stated in the Torah - and answers 'it is from here', from our 23:3, Abraham rising from before his dead. This is a case-anchored law reaching back to claim a verse: the bridge running INTO the reading rather than out of it.

check.note: A testing-shelf ruling naming this narrative verse as its derivation; the direction of travel is the point.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:4; Bereshit Rabbah 58:8
claim_en: THE CAVE IS GIVEN A STANDING OCCUPANT REGISTRY. The place-name is read as 'the doubled one' and tripled: its value doubled in all eyes, the reward of those buried in it doubled, and R. Abahu's reading that the first man's height was folded to lie in it. Around that sits a fixed roster - four righteous residents, four circumcised there, and four patriarchal couples buried there: the first man and his wife, Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Leah. The chain is not describing a grave but maintaining an occupancy list for a named place.

check.note: A place entity carrying a fixed roster of occupants across the corpus; world-fact shaped.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:5
claim_en: A CAUSE OF DEATH SUPPLIED BY JUXTAPOSITION, WITH ITS OWN OBJECTION RECORDED. Asked where Abraham CAME FROM at 23:2, the chain answers: from Mount Moriah - Sarah died of grief over the binding, the cause carried by nothing but the placement of the binding immediately before 'Sarah's lifetime'. R. Yosei's chronological objection is recorded rather than removed, and it is the objection that forces the Moriah answer. A cross-block wire: gen_38's altar is read as the efficient cause of this block's first verb.

check.note: A causal claim resting on textual adjacency alone, preserved together with the objection that constrains it.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 79:7
claim_en: THE PURCHASE IS ENROLLED AS STANDING TITLE AGAINST A FUTURE CLAIM. R. Yudan bar Simon names three places of which the nations can never say 'they are stolen in your hands', because each was bought on the record: this cave, the Temple site bought by David, and Joseph's burial plot bought by Jacob. Our weighing at 23:16 is cited as the deed. The chain is using a narrative conveyance as evidence in an argument it expects to have.

check.note: A narrative sale read as an evidentiary instrument in an anticipated future dispute.

source: Onkelos Genesis 23:6; Bereshit Rabbah 43:5
claim_en: ONE HONORIFIC, TWO SOLUTIONS, ONE DECLARED SHELF. At 23:6 the Hittites call Abraham a prince of God. Onkelos refuses the divine word as a mortal's epithet and converts the title to standing - 'you are RESPECTED BEFORE THE LORD in our midst'. The midrash leg of the same declared reading takes the identical words as a coronation formula, an acclamation from a consensus platform. Neither cites the other, and the two members of the spine solve one problem in two incompatible ways.

check.note: The two members of the declared reading treating one phrase by different devices.

source: Onkelos Genesis 23:16; Bereshit Rabbah 58:7
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION APPLIES A WEIGHT TABLE THE MIDRASH STATES. R. Chanina's rule that the Torah's shekels are selas is stated in the chain; Onkelos, without citing it, renders our 'four hundred shekels of silver' as four hundred SELAS - the table applied rather than quoted. The same verse's 'current with the merchant' becomes 'accepted as merchandise in every province', writing the universal-currency reading into the rendering. Two independent members of the declared reading converging on one verse's economics.

check.note: A translation silently applying a conversion table another member of the shelf states outright.

source: Onkelos Genesis 23:13; Onkelos Genesis 23:8
claim_en: THE BARGAINING IDIOM IS CONVERTED INTO OFFER AND ACCEPTANCE. Every 'hear me' and 'hear us' across the negotiation is rendered ACCEPT me, ACCEPT us, and the notorious broken clause of 23:13 is smoothed to 'if you will do me a kindness, accept me'. The buffer is not only avoiding an idiom; it is supplying conveyance vocabulary, so that the deal reads in the translation as a sequence of offers and acceptances.

check.note: A consistent lexical substitution across one negotiation that imports procedural vocabulary.

source: Kiddushin 2a:3-5, 4b:2-4, 11b:4-6
claim_en: THE BETROTHAL MONEY MACHINE. Tractate Kiddushin's opening derivation seated on the purchase: money betrothal by taking-taking from the field of Ephron ('I have given the silver of the field — take from me'), with the baraita's no-taking-except-silver route and the deflectable a-fortiori that made the verse necessary; taking-called-acquisition from 'the field that Abraham acquired'; the Beit Hillel peruta challenge resolved — the verse powers the MEDIUM, never the amount; and the two-grade currency table (fixed Torah silver Tyrian, the sages' provincial). Filed F-118, auto-seated (round 32, the betrothal block).

source: Bava Batra 69b:1 + Bekhorot 50a:8
claim_en: THE DEED FILE ON THE PURCHASE. The deed's border clause drafted from 'in all its border round about' (boundaries-from-the-Torah, Rav Mesharshiya), and Ephron's silver the recorded EXCEPTION to the three-corpus currency table — plain yet centenaria, by 'current with the merchant.' Filed F-128, auto-seated (round 34, the inheritance block).

source: Sanhedrin 46b:20-22
claim_en: THE EULOGY QUESTION OPENS ON THIS VERSE. Living's honor or dead's — the sugya's first proof is Abraham's eulogy for Sarah, deflected (Sarah is pleased that Abraham is honored through her); proof and deflection both kept as the question runs. Filed F-137, auto-seated (round 35, the courts block).

source: Berakhot 18a:3
claim_en: THE MOURNER-BEFORE-BURIAL EXEMPTION. Exempt from Shema, prayer, tefillin and every obligation — Rav Ashi's as-if-before-him status from the doubled from-before token at 23:3-4. Filed F-196, auto-seated (round 41, the kindness block).

source: Kiddushin 2a:4-5, 4b:3 (the betrothal block, credited); Bava Batra 69b:1, Bekhorot 50a:8 (the inheritance block, credited); Bava Metzia 87a:3; Berakhot 18a:3; Sanhedrin 46b:21; Eruvin 53a:4; Sotah 13a:9; Bava Kamma 93a:3; Rosh Hashanah 16b:5; Mishnah Kiddushin 1:1, 1:5, 1:6, Bava Metzia 4:9, Bava Batra 3:1, Bekhorot 8:7, 8:10
claim_en: THE PURCHASE RUNS THE THREE MODES: Gen 23 compiled in cold_run_family.py — Mishnah Kiddushin 1:5's money, deed, and possession as the chapter's three acts (the silver weighed, the record before the gate, the burial), the tractate opening on this field; 'current with the merchant' the phrase's only seat and the currency grade; no overreaching on land by call; the holding of a grave at five seats with the jubilee engine's tenure by call; the deed restated at 49:30 and 50:13 and cited at the burial; the onen's window from 'my dead before me'.
